large differences in risk allele frequency (RAF) for a set of SNPs that influence susceptibility to cardiovascular disease were noted among populations of varying origin.
large differences in allele frequencies for 158 common SNPs that are associated with cardiovascular disease risk were noted between the populations of the major geographic regions.

large differences in risk allele frequency (RAF) for a set of 158 common SNPs that affect risk of cardiovascular disease are noted between major world populations and that these differences may be due to selection or demographic factors.

the genetic basis of human variation and the genetic basis of common disease.
the study of human populations, their genetic variation, and how that variation is influenced by evolutionary and demographic processes, as well as by natural selection.
the study of the distribution of genetic variation among human populations, and its relationship with the geographic origin of the populations and with the prevalence of diseases.

there are differences in allele frequencies for some of the cardiovascular SNPs in different populations, which could be due to population specific selection, but the majority are not.

geographic variation in allele frequencies of common SNPs associated with cardiovascular disease is substantial and that some of these SNPs may be under selection in different populations.
